New Construction Proposal Intake

A complete, process walkthrough of the New Construction (NC) Proposal Intake process in the NYC HPD PIMS system — from the Development Team’s proposal submission on the external portal through HPD’s internal review, DASA committee review, and entry into the project pipeline.

This guide is written for people who are new to both Salesforce and the New Construction intake process. It follows one proposal end to end so you can see what each screen does and what to expect next.

Tip: click any screenshot to enlarge it for a closer look.

About This Guide

The New Construction Proposal Intake lets a Development Team propose a project to be built using HPD’s New Construction subsidy programs (for example ELLA, SARA, Supportive Housing, or Mix & Match). A proposal can begin two ways:

  • Inquiry first — submit a general New Construction inquiry, which HPD can review and advance to a full proposal.
  • Bypass the inquiry — go directly to the full proposal submission. This guide follows the bypass path and takes one proposal all the way to a pipeline project.

Login is not covered here. Each part of the guide begins from the screen you see immediately after signing in.

Purpose of This Guide

This document is a hands-on training reference for the New Construction Proposal Intake. Each step pairs an actual application screenshot with a clear Action (what to do) and Result (what to expect). Where helpful, steps reference the corresponding step in the Visio future-state process flow for traceability.

Who Should Use This Guide

  • Project Sponsors / Development Teams (and their consultants and attorneys) who submit proposals on the external portal.
  • NC Intake staff who review and process proposals — Project Managers, Deputy Directors, Directors, and the Assistant Commissioner of Planning & Predevelopment.
  • Office of Neighborhood Strategies (ONS) — Borough Planners and Borough Planning Directors, and the Land Use & Policy / Climate & Social Resiliency teams.
  • DASA Committee members who review referred proposals.
  • New PIMS / Salesforce users who need a guided, plain-language introduction.

Before You Begin

  • A valid PIMS account with the appropriate permissions (external portal access for applicants, the relevant role/queue for HPD staff).
  • The full proposal package ready to upload — for example Appraisal, Budget, Community Support, Market Study, Organizational Chart, Purchase and Sale Agreement, Schematic Designs, underwriting documentation, and a zoning analysis.
  • Key project facts on hand — location and elected officials, unit and area counts, income mix, financing programs, zoning/FAR, and acquisition details.
  • A supported web browser (latest Google Chrome recommended) and a stable connection.

Process at a Glance

The New Construction Proposal Intake follows this overall path:

  • 1Developer submits a proposal from the external portal (inquiry optional / bypassed)
  • 2HPD assigns a Project Manager; automatic review tasks are created
  • 3Proposal Review — organizational background, site control, due diligence, resiliency
  • 4Threshold Review — sole-source criteria & DASA referral decision
  • 5DASA Eligibility — Assistant Commissioner recommends submission
  • 6DASA Committee Review — committee records its decision (multiple rounds supported)
  • 7Approved proposal advances to Pipeline — a Project record is generated

Part A — The External PIMS Portal (Development Team)

A New Construction proposal is submitted by the Development Team on the external PIMS Portal. This guide bypasses the inquiry stage and submits a full proposal. After signing in, follow the steps below.

Step 1: Open the PIMS Portal Home

Action Sign in to the external PIMS Portal. On the Home page, the My Inquiries card lists your inquiries and the My Proposals card lists your proposals. To begin a new inquiry, click Apply Now in the My Inquiries card.

Result The portal Home page opens, giving you a single place to track your inquiries, proposals, requests, and projects. Clicking Apply Now starts a new New Construction inquiry.

Process map reference: Visio Step 1 — Submit Initial Proposal Inquiry.

Step 2: Choose the Inquiry Type

Action Two options are offered — New Construction Inquiry and Expression of Interest. Under New Construction Inquiry, click Complete Form.

Result The New Construction Inquiry screen opens.

Step 3: Bypass the Inquiry (Go Directly to Proposal Submission)

Action The Before You Begin panel explains that this form is for general inquiries about HPD New Construction subsidy programs. Because we are submitting a full proposal, click Bypass Inquiry — Go Directly to Proposal Submission.

Result A full proposal package (completed intake form, underwriting documentation, schematic plans, and a zoning analysis) is expected. Selecting Bypass opens the New Construction Proposal Intake form. The inquiry stage is optional — a developer can instead submit an inquiry first and convert it to a proposal later.

Process map reference: Visio Step 6 — Bypass Inquiry Stage.

Step 4: Read the Privacy Statement

Action The proposal intake form opens on the Privacy Statement step. Read the statement and click Next. The step tracker on the right shows all steps: Privacy Statement, Project Detail, Entities Information, Project Summary & Location, Zoning & Design, Acquisition Information, Documents, and Confirmation.

Result The form advances to the Project Detail step.

Step 5: Complete the Project Detail

Action Add the information in the fields accordingly and click Next. (The Date of Proposal Submission is auto-generated and can be edited if needed.)

Result The core project details and the developer’s affordable-housing experience are captured.

Process map reference: Visio Step 5 — Submit Proposal Intake Form.

Step 6: Add a New Entity

Action On the Entities Information step, click Add New Entity. Note the Application Number shown on the right (for example IA-0000000578) — the form saves automatically, so keep this number for reference.

Result The Entity Details form opens. The application already has a unique Application Number even before final submission.

Step 7: Enter Entity Details and the First Contact

Action Complete the Entity Details — Role, Legal Name, TIN/EIN Number, and address — then enter the first Entity Contact (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone).

Result The entity’s details and first contact are entered. Use the + button beside the contact to add more.

Step 7.1: Add Additional Contacts as Required

Action Click the + button to add more Entity Contacts. You can add multiple contacts as required — enter each contact’s First Name, Last Name, Email, and Phone — then click Save.

Result All required contacts are added to the entity and saved. There is no single-contact limit — capture as many contacts as the entity needs.

Step 8: Review the Added Entity

Action The saved entity appears in the Application Entities list, showing Legal Name, Role, TIN/EIN, Address, and Entity Contacts. Add more entities if needed, then click Next.

Result All application entities are listed. You can edit an entity with the pencil icon or add more before continuing.

Step 9: Complete Project Summary, Location & Financing

Action Fill in the location and elected-official fields, building and unit details (buildings, stories, affordable/market/total units, GSF, bedroom mix, super’s unit), the Describe Income Mix narrative, and the Financing Information section (Proposed HPD Financing Program, LIHTC, tax exemption, other credits, incentives, and anticipated social-service program). Click Next.

Result The complete project summary, location, and financing profile is captured for review.

Step 10: Complete Zoning & Design

Action Enter Zoning & Design details — Lot SF, Total Building GSF, Maximum/Proposed FAR, Zoning District, Inclusionary Housing program, and the Climate Resiliency and Environmental Information questions (floodplain, heat vulnerability, Phase I, E-Designations, demolition, etc.). Click Next.

Result The zoning, design, climate-resiliency, and environmental profile is recorded — this information helps HPD flag any land-use or resiliency review needs.

Step 11: Complete Acquisition Information

Action Enter Acquisition Information — current/previous owner, current land use, acquisition date and price, appraised value, ownership type, mortgages, financing, and site-history questions (city ownership, deed restrictions, faith-based involvement, assemblage). Use the free-text box to explain site history and site-control status. Click Next.

Result The acquisition and site-control details are captured, including whether the site was ever City-owned — a key factor in the DASA / sole-source determination.

Process map reference: Visio Step 7a.2 — Review Site Control, History and Acquisition.

Step 12: Review the Document Checklist

Action On the Documents step, review the Document Checklist — Appraisal, Budget, Community Support, Market Study, Organizational Chart, Purchase and Sale Agreement, Schematic Designs, and more. Each required item is marked with a red asterisk and starts as Pending. Click the upload icon on a document line.

Result The checklist shows every document required for this proposal. Required items must be uploaded before submission.

Step 13: Upload the Required Documents

Action In the Upload Documents pop-up, drag and drop files or click Choose Files (max 10 MB per file), then click Upload.

Result The selected files are attached to the document line.

Step 14: Confirm Documents and Submit

Action When every required document shows Submitted, review the checklist and click Submit.

Result All required documents are attached and the proposal is ready to submit to HPD.

Step 15: Submission Confirmation

Action Read the confirmation message and note the application number. From here you can click Go to Home or View Proposal. Click View Proposal to review the submitted proposal.

Result PIMS confirms the application was submitted successfully and displays its application number (for example IA-0000000578).

Step 16: Review the Submitted Proposal

Action Review the submitted proposal.

Result The proposal record opens (status Draft on the portal) showing Project Information and tabbed sections — Details, Project Summary & Location, Acquisition Information, Financing Information, Zoning & Design, Climate Resiliency, and more — for reference.

Part B — The Internal PIMS Application (HPD Staff)

Once submitted, the proposal is processed by HPD staff in the internal PIMS application (Salesforce). As the proposal moves through review, the record’s status path updates and PIMS automatically creates tasks and notifications for the responsible teams.

Step 17: Open the HPD Staff Home

Action Sign in to the internal PIMS application. This is the Home tab, which shows Action Items, Active Modules, and Pending Milestones in My Queue. Click the dropdown (arrow) menu beside Home, which opens the list of objects.

Result The Home page gives HPD staff a single view of items pending their approval, assigned modules, and milestones. Clicking the dropdown beside Home opens the list of objects available in PIMS. Note: this area is still under progress and may change based on the process.

Step 18: Select the Applications Object

Action From the list of objects, select Applications.

Result The Applications object opens.

Step 19: Open a List View

Action The Applications object opens on All Applications. Click the list-view selector arrow at the top and choose the New Construction Intake list view.

Result The New Construction Intake list view is selected.

Step 20: Open the New Construction Intake Record

Action Select the New Construction Intake list view. Locate the submitted application — here IA-0000000578, Grand Concourse Commons — and click its Application ID to open it.

Result The New Construction Intake list shows all proposals submitted from the portal. The selected application record opens.

Step 21: Review the Application and Assign a PM

Action Review the application. The status path at the top tracks the record’s stage (Submitted → Proposal Review → Threshold Review → DASA Eligibility → DASA Review → AC Review → In Pipeline / Rejected), and Guidance for Success tells you what to do next. Use the View Proposal tab (Details, Zoning & Design, Entities, Locations, Source & Uses, etc.) and the Documents tab to review. To assign a Project Manager, click the pencil next to Project Manager.

Result The application opens in Submitted status. Guidance instructs you to verify attachments and assign a PM to proceed.

Process map reference: Visio Step 6a — Assign Project Manager.

Step 22: Assign the Project Manager

Action In the Key Fields editor, set the Project Manager and AC Expedite to Pipeline, then click Save. The flow changes based on the AC Expedite to Pipeline value — here we select No so we can walk through the complete process.

Result The Project Manager is assigned to the application.

Step 23: Automatic Review Tasks Are Created

Action No action needed here — observe the Activity timeline. When the PM is assigned, PIMS automatically creates and notifies the assigned person of review tasks: Due Diligence Review, Review Site Control, History and Acquisition, and Review Organizational Background Experience.

Result The assigned PM receives automatic tasks covering the concurrent proposal-review activities. The PM logs into the PIMS portal, completes each assigned task, and clicks the checkbox to mark it complete.

Process map reference: Visio Steps 7a.1–7a.3 — Proposal Review activities.

Step 24: Set the Climate Resiliency & Prior Ownership Flags

Action Once the PM completes the assigned tasks, the PM updates the Climate Resiliency and Prior City/Public Ownership values accordingly. Back in Key Fields, click the pencil next to Climate Resiliency Concerns and Prior City/Public Ownership.

Result The key-field editor opens for the resiliency and prior-ownership flags.

Step 25: Save the Key-Field Flags

Action Set Climate Resiliency Concerns and Prior City/Public Ownership, then click Save. (Select the values that apply — here both are set to Yes.)

Result The flags are saved. Setting these values triggers automatic notifications to the Land Use & Policy and Climate & Social Resiliency teams.

Process map reference: Visio Steps 9a / 9b — Notify LUP / Resiliency Team.

Step 26: Proposal Review Begins

Action The record advances to Proposal Review. Guidance now reads “Complete all checklist items below. Review cannot proceed until all are checked.” In the Activity timeline you can see the automatic Proposal Flagged: Prior City/Public Ownership and Proposal Flagged for Climate Resiliency Review notifications. Open the Proposal Review tab.

Result The status is now Proposal Review, and the relevant teams have been notified. The Proposal Review checklist is ready to complete.

Process map reference: Visio Step 7a — Start Proposal Review.

Step 27: Complete the Proposal Review Checklist

Action Update the fields according to the project requirement, then click Save.

Result The proposal-review determinations are recorded. Most items must be complete before a determination can be made.

Process map reference: Visio Step 10b — PM Completes Proposal Review.

Step 28: Record the DASA Determination

Action After the checklist is saved, a DASA Determination section appears. Click the pencil next to DASA Determination?

Result The DASA Determination field opens for editing.

Process map reference: Visio Step 11 — DASA Determination.

Step 29: Set the DASA Determination

Action Set DASA Determination? (here Yes, referring the proposal for DASA review) and click Save.

Result The DASA determination is recorded and the record advances.

Step 30: Threshold Review Begins

Action The record advances to Threshold Review. Guidance reads “Evaluate all threshold criteria. Determine DASA referral decision.” New Key Fields appear — Project meet Sole Source Criteria?, Referred for DASA Committee Review, and Any Additional Threshold Issues? Open the Threshold Review tab.

Result The status is now Threshold Review, ready for the ONS / Borough Planning threshold evaluation.

Process map reference: Visio Steps 12–14b — Borough Planning / Threshold Review.

Step 31: Open the Threshold Review Fields

Action On the Threshold Review tab, click the pencil to edit the threshold fields (starting with Current deed restrictions).

Result The Threshold Review editor opens.

Step 32: Complete the Threshold Review and Sole Source Rationale

Action Fill in the details accordingly, then click Save.

Result The threshold determination and sole-source rationale are recorded.

Process map reference: Visio Step 7b.1 — Assess for Sole Source Eligibility.

Step 33: DASA Eligibility Begins

Action The record advances to DASA Eligibility. Guidance reads “Confirm DASA referral. If referred, schedule DASA Committee meeting.” The saved Sole Source Rationale is visible on the Threshold Review tab. Open the DASA Eligibility tab.

Result The status is now DASA Eligibility, ready for the Assistant Commissioner recommendation.

Step 34: Open the AC Recommendation Field

Action The AC logs into the PIMS portal to make this update. On the DASA Eligibility tab, click the pencil next to AC Recommends DASA Submission.

Result The AC-recommendation field opens for editing.

Process map reference: Visio Step 15 — AC Provides Formal Approval for DASA Submission.

Step 35: Record the AC Recommendation

Action Set AC Recommends DASA Submission (here Yes) and click Save.

Result The Assistant Commissioner’s recommendation is recorded and the record advances.

Step 36: DASA Review Begins — Notifications Sent

Action The record advances to DASA Review. Guidance reads “Record committee meeting and decision. Multiple review rounds are supported.” The Activity timeline shows automatic AC recommends submission to the DASA Committee notifications to committee members. Open the DASA Review tab.

Result The status is now DASA Review, and the DASA Committee has been notified.

Process map reference: Visio Steps 16–17 — ONS Prepares DASA Materials / DASA Committee Meets.

Step 37: Add a DASA Committee Review

Action On the DASA Review tab, the Application Reviews list is empty. Click New to record a committee review round.

Result A blank DASA Committee Review form opens. Multiple review rounds can be added.

Process map reference: Visio Step 18 — DASA Committee Review.

Step 38: Open the DASA Committee Review Form

Action The DASA Committee Review form opens. Fill in all the details.

Result The empty review form is displayed; required fields are marked and validated on submit.

Step 39: Complete the DASA Committee Review

Action Fill in all the details, then click Submit.

Result The DASA Committee review round is captured with the committee’s decision.

Step 40: DASA Committee Review Submitted

Action A confirmation appears: “Your DASA Committee Review is Submitted.” Click Done.

Result The review round is saved and added to the Application Reviews list.

Step 41: Record the Committee Decision

Action The Application Reviews list now shows the submitted review (Proposed Uses, Date of Committee Meeting, Status, and DASA Committee decision). To record the overall outcome, click the pencil next to Has proposal approved by DASA Committee?

Result The completed committee review is listed, and the overall DASA Committee Decision field is ready to set.

Step 42: Set the DASA Committee Decision

Action Set Has proposal approved by DASA Committee? (here Approved) and click Save.

Result The DASA Committee decision is recorded and the proposal advances.

Step 43: Proposal Advances to Pipeline

Action The record advances to In Pipeline. Guidance reads “Proposal is now in pipeline. Update project status as development progresses.” A Projects related list now shows the new project (Grand Concourse Commons, with the assigned PM and Sole Source = Yes), and a new task, Complete Proposal-to-Pipeline Checklist, is created for the PM. Open that task.

Result Once DASA approval is recorded, the proposal becomes a pipeline project — a Project record is generated and the proposal-to-pipeline checklist task is assigned.

Process map reference: Visio Steps 19 / 11a.2 — ONS Documents Approval / Proposal-to-Pipeline.

Step 44: Open the Proposal-to-Pipeline Checklist Task

Action Open the Complete Proposal-to-Pipeline Checklist task. Review the task details (Assigned To, Related To the application, and Comments — e.g. “Attach Recommendation Email to AC”), then click Mark Complete.

Result The task detail opens, showing what the PM must do to close out the proposal-to-pipeline step.

Step 45: Complete the Checklist Task

Action The task Status updates to Completed. Close the task tab to return to the application.

Result The proposal-to-pipeline checklist task is complete.

Step 46: Open the Linked Project

Action Back on the application (now In Pipeline), the completed task shows as struck through and the Projects related list shows the linked project. Click Grand Concourse Commons to open the project.

Result The application is now in pipeline with its linked project, and the checklist task is complete.

Step 47: The New Pipeline Project

Action The Project record opens — Grand Concourse Commons — with tabs for Details, Programs, Buildings, Entities, Project Fundings, Modules, Units & Affordability, Sources & Uses, and more. Key fields (Project Manager, Sole Source, Borough, Project Type, description, unit projections) carry over from the proposal.

Result The proposal is now a project in pipeline with its own Project record and Project ID, ready to move into the next phase of the development lifecycle.

Process map reference: Visio — Project in Pipeline (unique Project ID generated).

Summary

In this guide you followed a New Construction proposal from start to finish. On the external portal, the Development Team bypassed the inquiry stage, completed the multi-step proposal intake (project detail and developer experience, entities, project summary & location, financing, zoning & design, and acquisition), uploaded the required documents, and submitted — receiving an application number. In the internal application, HPD assigned a Project Manager (which auto-generated review tasks), completed the Proposal Review, made the DASA determination, completed the Threshold Review with a sole-source rationale, recorded the Assistant Commissioner’s DASA recommendation, and captured the DASA Committee’s decision. Once approved, the proposal advanced to In Pipeline, generating a Project record and a proposal-to-pipeline checklist — moving the proposal into the project pipeline.

Notes & Disclaimers

  • This guide follows the bypass-inquiry path for a project that is referred for DASA review and approved. Other paths (inquiry-first, rejection, revisions requested, discussion without vote, previously conveyed / sole-source land) differ — refer to the Visio future-state process flow.
  • Several review stages support multiple rounds and concurrent tasks; the exact fields and notifications depend on the proposal’s characteristics (prior city ownership, climate resiliency, sole source, etc.).
  • Screens, field names, and buttons may vary by role, permissions, browser, resolution, and future PIMS updates. This process is still evolving and may change.
  • Names, application numbers, and data shown are from a training/sandbox environment and are for illustration only.
